clips.title: DRI Guide: Directly Responsible Individuals (Tettra)
clips.why: A 44-second idea from management that this lesson builds into code: every piece of work has exactly one person who owns it.
look: One named owner per piece of work, not a group.
Ask yourself who owns RH-1234 while Nova waits, and who owns it after the wait ends.
clips.after: Handing the ticket back to the requester is how the platform makes sure RH-1234 always has one person as its owner, even when Nova stops waiting.

clips.title: Jira Best Practices - Assignee field vs User Picker field
clips.why: A Jira consultant compares the assignee field with extra user fields for approval steps, which is the choice behind "assigned to Nova means Nova's turn".
look: The question he asks: should an approval step reassign the issue, or store the approver in another field?
How automation can change the assignee as work moves from one person to the next.
Think about what our poll reads: only the assignee.
clips.after: Our poll asks Jira for tickets assigned to Nova, so the assignee is both "whose turn it is" and the switch that starts runs; that is why every ending assigns the ticket back.

clips.title: Temporal Live Coding Demo: Handling Failures & Human Interaction
clips.why: A live coding demo adds a timer that races a signal, the exact mechanism inside waitForPerson.
look: The signal and the timer race: whichever happens first decides what the workflow does next.
The timer is durable, so the workflow can wait without anything running.
Compare with waitForPerson, which runs this race twice: once for the reminder, once for the hand-back.
clips.after: waitForPerson is two of these races in a row, with Stop added to the condition so a Stop always wins.

clips.title: The Human Is an Async API — Melanie Warrick, Temporal
clips.why: A short answer to the question behind every wait in this lesson: when should an agent ask a person at all?
look: Listen for when she thinks a person belongs in the loop, and when not.
Ask yourself what each question or reminder costs the person who receives it.
clips.after: The same reasoning sets Nova's rule for reminders: one reminder per wait, then a clear hand-back, so Nova's messages stay worth reading.

practice.q: handBack gives the ticket back. Finish the line that matters most, so the poll leaves the ticket alone.
practice.hint: The person who handed the ticket to Nova, carried in the run's input.
practice.why: As long as Nova is the assignee, the poll starts or joins a run every minute. Making the requester the assignee again takes the ticket out of the poll, and it gives the ticket a person as its owner.

practice.q: Which first wait in waitForPerson lets a Stop end the wait at once?

options.why: This only wakes up when the person acts. A Stop would wait for the reminder time first.
condition() re-checks its function whenever the run's state changes, so the stop signal ends the wait the moment it arrives.
sleep cannot be interrupted by a signal, so a Stop would still wait a full day, and the person's answer would wait too.

practice.q: You are on holiday. Put what happens to RH-1234 in order.
items: Nova posts the plan and releases the lite VM
After 1 day, one reminder in the thread mentions you
After 3 days, Nova posts why and assigns the ticket back to you; the run ends as parked
Every minute the poll runs, but RH-1234 no longer matches assigned to Nova
You come back and assign RH-1234 to Nova again
The poll starts a fresh run nova:RH-1234, and the branch and notes are still there
practice.why: The hand-back takes the ticket out of the poll's query, and only a person's new assignment puts it back.

practice.q: Nova asked a question 10 minutes ago and nobody has answered yet. What happens now?

options.text: The VM is parked: stopped with its disk kept, while the run keeps waiting
options.why: Parking a VM saves money during a wait. The run, the session and the work go on when the answer comes.

options.text: The ticket is handed back to the requester
options.why: That is parking a ticket, which happens only after 2 days without an answer.
The reminder for a question comes after 1 day, not after 10 minutes.

practice.q: The poll treats a change of assignee away from Nova as Stop. Nova's own hand-back also changes the assignee. What must the rule check?

options.text: Who made the change: anyone except Nova means Stop
options.why: Nova's own assign-back is the run ending as planned; a person moving the ticket is a Stop.

options.text: Whether the new assignee is the requester
options.why: A person might also stop Nova by assigning the ticket to the requester, so the new assignee does not tell you who acted.

options.text: Nothing: a second Stop on a finished run does no harm
options.why: Usually true, but the stop signal could reach a fresh run that a person just started. Checking who made the change avoids that.

practice.q: You press Stop in RH-1234's thread while Nova is building on a full VM. Put what happens in order.
items: The Slack app sends the stop signal to nova:RH-1234, with your name
The harness saves a checkpoint commit on nova/RH-1234
The VM is released, and the slot goes back
Nova posts why and makes you the assignee again
The poll no longer matches RH-1234, and the branch and notes wait for the next run
practice.why: Stop always wins, and like every ending it saves the work and gives the ticket back, so the poll leaves the ticket alone until a person assigns it to Nova again.
